title: Negative numbers and order of operations
blurb: Apply the sign rules for negative numbers and work any expression in the correct order, left to right where ranks tie.
question: A patient's fluid balance is −250 mL at the start of a shift, and a classmate says 20 − 12 ÷ 4 × 2 equals 4. How do you handle the negative balance, and what is the expression's correct value?

teach.body: Formally, integers are the whole numbers and their opposites (…, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, …), and the order of operations is the agreed sequence for evaluating an expression: grouping, exponents, multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction. In plain English: learn a few sign rules so negatives never trip you, and always work an expression in the same order so everyone gets the same answer.

head: Situation
Rule
Example
rows: Subtract sizes; sign of larger size
teach.caption: "Size" means absolute value, the distance from 0: |−7| = 7.
Several factors: an even number of negatives gives a positive product, an odd number a negative one.

items: −7 + 4: different signs, so 7 − 4 = 3, and the larger size (7) is negative: −3.
6 − (−2): subtracting a negative is adding, so 6 + 2 = 8.
Check −7 + 4 on a number line: start at −7, move 4 right, land on −3. ✓

teach.body: Multiplication and division share one rank, and so do addition and subtraction. Within a rank, work strictly left to right. So 8 ÷ 2 × 4 = 4 × 4 = 16, not 8 ÷ 8 = 1, and 10 − 3 + 2 = 9, not 10 − 5 = 5. The letters in PEMDAS list M before D and A before S only because a word needs an order; they are not a ranking.

items: Check: doing 4 × 2 first gives 20 − 1.5 = 18.5, a different (wrong) answer, so order matters.

teach.caption: A basic calculator may work left to right as you type, so enter one step at a time.

teach.text: (−3)² = (−3)(−3) = 9, but −3² = −(3²) = −9: the exponent applies before the negation unless the negative is inside parentheses. And never do multiplication before a division that sits to its left.

teach.body: Destiny Clark, a nursing applicant shadowing on a medical unit, sees a fluid balance of −250 mL at the start of the shift. During the shift the patient takes in 900 mL and puts out 550 mL. New balance: −250 + 900 − 550. Work left to right: −250 + 900 = 650; 650 − 550 = 100 mL. Check: net change is 900 − 550 = +350, and −250 + 350 = 100. ✓

items: Same signs add and keep the sign; different signs subtract sizes and take the larger size's sign.
Subtracting a negative is adding a positive.
× and ÷: same signs positive, different signs negative; count negatives for longer products.
Order: grouping, exponents, × and ÷ left to right, + and − left to right.

summary: You can now add, subtract, multiply and divide negative numbers with the right sign and evaluate expressions in the correct order of operations, working left to right where ranks tie. You can also explain why a basic calculator or a skipped step gives the wrong value.

whyNot.1: 5 drops the negative sign on the 8: 8 + 3 − 6.

A.why: Exponent first: 3² = 9. Then ÷ and × left to right: 24 ÷ 4 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12. Then add: 12 + 9 = 21.

whyNot.0: 12 multiplies 4 × 2 before dividing: 24 ÷ 8 + 9 = 12. Division comes first because it is on the left.
whyNot.2: 225 works left to right and squares the whole result: (12 + 3)² = 15².

A.why: (−2)(−5) = 10; 10 × (−3) = −30; −30 ÷ (−6) = 5. Four negatives (even) give a positive result.

whyNot.1: −5 gets the sign wrong: there are four negative numbers, an even count, so the result is positive.
whyNot.2: −30 is the product of the first three numbers, before dividing by −6.

B.q: Which expression has a value of −16?
B.why: In −4² the exponent applies first: 4² = 16, then the negative: −16.

whyNot.0: (−4)² = (−4)(−4) = 16; the parentheses put the negative inside the square.
whyNot.2: (−2)⁴ = 16: four negative factors, an even number, give a positive.
whyNot.3: −2 × −8 = 16: two negatives multiply to a positive.

B.q: A patient's fluid balance at 0700 is −320 mL. During the shift, intake is 1,150 mL and output is 940 mL. What is the fluid balance at the end of the shift?
B.why: Intake adds, output subtracts: −320 + 1,150 − 940. Left to right: −320 + 1,150 = 830; 830 − 940 = −110 mL.

whyNot.2: 530 drops the negative on the starting balance: 320 + 1,150 − 940.

B.why: Multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12. Then add and subtract left to right: 50 − 20 = 30; 30 + 5 = 35; 35 − 12 = 23.

whyNot.0: 13 adds 20 + 5 before subtracting from 50; addition does not outrank subtraction.
whyNot.1: 128 works strictly left to right, multiplying last: (50 − 20 + 5 − 3) × 4.
whyNot.3: 37 subtracts the group 20 + 5 − 12 from 50 as if it were in parentheses.

whyNot.0: 3 subtracts 10 − 4 first: 6 × 4 ÷ 8. Multiplication comes before subtraction.
whyNot.1: 12 squares −2 as −4, giving 4 × (−4) ÷ 8 = −2 and 10 − (−2) = 12; a negative squared is positive.
whyNot.3: 14 squares the 3 before working the parentheses: 1 − 9 = −8, so 10 − (−4) = 14.

C.q: At 6 a.m. the temperature in Duluth was −14°F. By noon it had risen 23°F, and by midnight it had fallen 17°F from the noon reading. What was the midnight temperature?

whyNot.0: 9°F is the noon temperature, an intermediate step.
whyNot.2: −54°F treats the rise as a fall: −14 − 23 − 17.

C.q: A student types 6 + 18 ÷ 3 × 2 − 4 into a basic calculator one key at a time and gets 12. What is the correct value of the expression?
C.why: Divide and multiply first, left to right: 18 ÷ 3 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12. Then 6 + 12 − 4 = 14.

whyNot.2: 12 is the calculator's left-to-right result, (6 + 18) ÷ 3 × 2 − 4, which ignores the order of operations.

reteach.title: Think like a thermometer
reteach.question: On a winter morning the thermometer reads −5°F. It warms up 12 degrees, then drops 15 degrees. How does reading a thermometer make the sign rules obvious?

blocks.h: Up is plus, down is minus
blocks.body: A thermometer is a number line standing up. Adding moves you up, subtracting moves you down. Start at −5 and warm up 12: you pass 0 after 5 degrees and keep going 7 more, landing on 7. Drop 15: you fall 7 degrees to 0 and 8 more, landing on −8. Subtracting a negative is like a cold front being canceled: removing a drop makes it warmer.

items: −5 + 12: different signs, 12 − 5 = 7, larger size is positive: 7.
7 − 15: same as 7 + (−15); different signs, 15 − 7 = 8, larger size is negative: −8.
The thermometer and the rules agree. ✓

blocks.text: −8 is colder than −5. On a number line, the farther left (or lower), the smaller the number.

explain.body: Change every subtraction to adding the opposite, then combine. Same signs: add sizes, keep the sign. Different signs: subtract sizes, keep the sign of the larger size.

test.why: − (−9) = + 9, so −15 + 9 + 4 = −15 + 13. Sizes: 15 − 13 = 2, and the larger size (15) is negative: −2.

whyNot.2: 2 gets the size right but takes the sign of the smaller size; 15 is larger and negative.
whyNot.3: −28 treats both the − (−9) and the + 4 as subtractions.

explain.body: Same signs give a positive, different signs give a negative. For a chain, count the negatives: even count positive, odd count negative.

whyNot.0: −3 has the wrong sign: dividing a negative by a negative gives a positive.
whyNot.1: −24 is the product before dividing by −8, an intermediate step.

explain.body: Grouping, then exponents, then × and ÷ together left to right, then + and − together left to right. In 40 ÷ 5 × 2 − 6, the division comes first because it is on the left.

test.why: Left to right for ÷ and ×: 40 ÷ 5 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16. Then 16 − 6 = 10.

whyNot.0: −2 multiplies 5 × 2 first: 40 ÷ 10 − 6. Division is on the left, so it comes first.

explain.body: Parentheses decide what is raised to the power. (−2)⁴ = 16 because the negative is inside; −2⁴ = −16 because only the 2 is raised. An odd power of a negative stays negative: (−2)³ = −8.

whyNot.1: −128 merges the terms into one power, −2⁷, by adding the exponents; that rule is for multiplying powers, not adding them.
